body.content: Scratch advisory context suggests that the standard result 12 relies on the implicit assumption of a single linear application of the percentage. A counterfactual test: If the problem were 'What is 15% of 80 over 2 periods?' the answer would be 80 × 1.15^2 = 105.8, not 12. This boundary highlights that compounding or time dimensions alter the operation from linear scaling to exponential growth. The covering principle for the standard result is the linearity of single-step scaling.
body.possible_next_move: Test if any non-linear interpretation of the problem text could be validly inferred, or if the linear reading is the only admissible one.
body.why_keep_this: To track the boundary conditions where standard percentage arithmetic fails and to ensure the decomposition methods are not blindly trusted.
